installer.secure_boot.enroll_note: Secure Boot: a computer with Secure Boot on starts this drive after the USOS key has been added once. Easiest: start USOS once with Secure Boot off and confirm "Add the key". With Secure Boot on: in MokManager choose Enroll key from disk -> USOS_ESP -> USOS-KEY.cer -> Continue -> Yes -> Reboot. See EFI\USOS\ENROLL-README.txt.
installer.mok.button: Add the USOS key on this computer
installer.mok.intro: USOS is signed with its own key. A computer with Secure Boot on starts USOS only after this key has been added once. No password is needed.
installer.mok.scope: The key is trusted only by shim and USOS, not by Windows, and the change applies only to this computer. Nothing is written to any drive.
installer.mok.already: The USOS key is already on this computer. Nothing needs to be done.
installer.mok.pending: Already prepared: MokManager will wait for you on the next start from the USOS drive.
installer.mok.secure_boot_off: Secure Boot is off on this computer. USOS starts as it is and offers to save its key on its home screen; after that Secure Boot can be turned on.
installer.mok.not_uefi: Windows on this computer was started in legacy BIOS (CSM) mode, so UEFI variables cannot be written. The key can only be enrolled on a computer that starts in UEFI mode.
installer.mok.no_privilege: Windows refused access to the UEFI variables. Start the installer as administrator.
installer.mok.failed: The MokManager wait could not be prepared: %s
installer.mok.cert_missing: The USOS key could not be read from the installer: %s
installer.mok.way1_title: Easiest: start USOS once with Secure Boot off
installer.mok.way1_text:
1. Restart into the BIOS settings and turn Secure Boot off.
2. Start the computer from the USOS drive and confirm "Add the key" on the USOS home screen.
3. Turn Secure Boot back on in the BIOS settings.
installer.mok.way1_note: Add the key BEFORE turning Secure Boot on: then shim's "Verification failed" screen never appears. This also works when the BIOS has no Secure Boot keys yet (Setup Mode). After turning Secure Boot on, install the default keys (Install default Secure Boot keys / Factory keys), including the Microsoft UEFI CA. On many boards Secure Boot needs CSM turned off.
installer.mok.way2_text: Click Prepare: the blue MokManager screen will then wait for you instead of counting down. Start the computer from the USOS drive and follow these steps:
installer.mok.tap_once: On a handheld tap each button once, do not hold it: a held button skips the screens.
installer.mok.clipped_hint: If the text of shim or MokManager looks cut off at the screen edge: turn off overscan on the monitor or TV ("Just Scan", "1:1", "Screen fit") and "Full Screen Logo" in the BIOS settings, or simply use way 1.
installer.mok.prepared: Prepared. Restart and start the computer from the USOS drive (the boot menu key is often F8, F11, F12 or Esc).

boot.sbinfo.how_line2: 2. In the blue MokManager screen choose Enroll key from disk -> USOS_ESP -> USOS-KEY.cer.
boot.sbinfo.how_line3: 3. Choose Continue -> Yes -> Reboot. No password is needed.
boot.sbinfo.how_line4: On a handheld tap each button once, do not hold it: a held button skips the screens.

boot.sbinfo.guide_first: Add the key now, before turning Secure Boot on: then the "Verification failed" screen never appears.

boot.profile.help.bypass: For hardware below the Windows 11 requirements. Microsoft does not support such installations; feature updates may need the bypass again.
boot.profile.help.computer: 1-15 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 and -, not only digits. Empty: USOS-XP on XP, a name chosen by Setup on newer Windows.
boot.profile.help.disable_wer: Vista and newer: Windows Error Reporting stays off (no problem reports are sent).
boot.profile.help.edition: Edition Setup installs, matched against the images of the chosen ISO (also across languages; Server: Core or Desktop Experience). Empty or not on the ISO: Setup shows its edition list.
boot.profile.help.key: Product key for {0} (XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX). Empty: Setup asks for it or offers the edition list.
boot.profile.help.keyboard: Keyboard layout of Windows. Same as the formats: the default keyboard of that language.
boot.profile.help.language: Language of Setup and of Windows; the installation media must contain it. Automatic: Setup asks.
boot.profile.help.local_account: Windows 8 and newer: create the accounts locally and hide the Microsoft account pages.
boot.profile.help.locale: Date, time, number and currency formats.
boot.profile.help.name: Name of the profile on this stick: 1-32 characters A-Z a-z 0-9, space, . _ -
boot.profile.help.network_location: Vista and 7: answer to the network location page. Work or Home: a private network; Public: the strictest firewall.
boot.profile.help.no_network: Windows 11: finish the setup without a network connection (BypassNRO).
boot.profile.help.password: Password of the accounts; empty means no password. It is stored as plain text on the stick.
boot.profile.help.protect_pc: Answer to the "Help protect Windows" page (Vista and newer). Off: no automatic updates until you turn them on.
boot.profile.help.remember_key: Off: the key is used until this computer restarts and is never written to the stick.
boot.profile.help.timezone: Automatic: the default of the installation media.
boot.profile.help.user: First local account, an administrator: 1-20 characters A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - and space.
boot.profile.manual.detail: Setup asks every question itself; no profile or file is used
boot.profile.problem.bad_characters: It contains characters that are not allowed here.
boot.profile.problem.bad_key_format: A product key has the form XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX.
boot.profile.problem.duplicate: A profile with this name exists already.
boot.profile.problem.only_digits: A computer name cannot be only digits.
boot.profile.problem.reserved_name: This is the name of a built-in Windows account.
boot.profile.problem.same_as_user: The second user must differ from the first.

boot.profile.missing.password: {0} needs a password of at least 7 characters with three of: capitals, small letters, digits, symbols. Without one Setup stops on the Administrator password page.
boot.profile.help.systems: The systems whose answer screen offers this profile. Profiles saved without this setting are offered for every Windows, never for Linux.
boot.profile.help.show_extensions: Explorer shows file name extensions such as .exe (for every new user).
boot.profile.help.show_hidden: Explorer shows hidden files and folders (for every new user); protected system files stay hidden.
boot.profile.help.no_autorun: AutoRun and AutoPlay stay off on every drive, USB sticks and CDs included (NoDriveTypeAutoRun).
boot.profile.help.disable_uac: Vista and 7: User Account Control off. Less safe: every program of an administrator runs with full rights.
boot.profile.help.skip_games: XP: the games are not installed. Vista and 7: the Games feature is turned off during Setup.
boot.profile.help.skip_msn: XP and Server 2003: MSN Explorer and Windows Messenger are not installed.
boot.profile.help.hide_outlook_express: XP and Server 2003: the Outlook Express shortcuts are removed; the program itself stays.
boot.profile.help.classic_start: XP: the Windows 2000 style Start menu for new users.
boot.profile.help.no_balloon_tips: XP and Server 2003: no balloon tips in the notification area; XP also skips the "Tour Windows XP" prompt.
boot.profile.help.no_sidebar: Vista: Windows Sidebar, 7: desktop gadgets, turned off by policy.
boot.profile.help.no_welcome_center: Vista: the Welcome Center does not open at every logon.
boot.profile.help.no_hibernation: Vista and 7: no hibernation and no hybrid sleep; the disk space of hiberfil.sys is freed.
boot.profile.help.theme: Theme of new users. XP: Windows Classic instead of Luna. 7: Windows Classic or Windows 7 Basic.
boot.profile.help.display: XP and Server 2003: 32-bit colour at this resolution when the display driver offers it. Automatic: unchanged; without a display driver (the VGA driver, e.g. through CSMWrap) Windows keeps its basic mode.
